newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt coffee sales seen key in '97 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt coffee sales seen key in '97 1st half.

text.p: Brazil has published its list of auctions of coffee stocks between January and June and already traders are beginning to discuss whether it should increase the size of sales, currently limited to 200,000 bags.
"I think for the market the government should announce the limit. Otherwise it could be anything," said Jorge Esteve, president of the Brazilian Association of Coffee Exporters.
When the government first announced its program for 1996/97 (July/June), it said that the size of each individual auction would depend on internal supply.

As a result, given the 1996/97 harvest has been continuing to arrive in quantity since the auctions began, sales have so far been much lower than the 200,000 bag limit, with the largest for 85,466 due to be held on November 20.
In fact since July, only 134,806 bags have been made available, of which 126,797 bags have been bought up.
Some traders now are anticipating that the government will have to increase the level of sales sharply to meet internal demands and export commitments in the first half of next year.

Working on the basis of nine million bags of exports in July to December, around 5.5 million bags for internal consumption and 1.65 million bags for soluble exports, this gives total demand in July to December of around 16.15 million bags.
If soluble exports are repeated in the first half of next year and domestic demand rises to six million bags, this already gives a figure of 23.8 million bags.
With regard to export availability in the first half of the year, much will depend on carry-over stocks into 1996/97, the real size of the crop and the size of auctions.
Allowing for November and December, government auctions in the second half of this year are likely to total 300,000 bags in total, giving 23.5 million bags.
Carry-over stocks into this year meanwhile are thought to be around 2.5 million bags, bringing the total down to 21 million.

If Brazil therefore wants to fulfill the six million bags of exports it has been alloted in the first half of next year by other producing nations, it will have to see significant sales by the government in the six month period.

Even if the 1996/97 crop is really 27.5 million bags as estimated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the government would still need to auction a total of two million bags in the first six months of next year to maintain what are seen as already minimum carry-over stocks of 2.5 million bags.
And obviously if the crop is lower, auction sales will have to be much higher - or Brazilian exports will suffer.
The key period is definitely going to be in the second quarter of 1997, analysts and traders said.

"Unless the government steps in, it looks as if the Brazilian market is going to be very tight and if exports are kept to a moderate level in the first quarter of next year, then the world market will be squeezed," said Lawrence Eagles, analyst at London trade house GNI.
A moderate level would be monthly exports of one million bags in January to March. This would leave virtually no coffee for export from Brazil in the second quarter, Eagles said.
